name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
life_summary: Dietrich Bonhoeffer was born in Breslau in 1906, grew up in Berlin from 1912, and completed a doctorate in theology at Berlin University in 1927. After passing his first theological examination in January 1928 he spent a year as vicar to the German congregation in Barcelona (February 1928 to February 1929), qualified as a university teacher in 1930, and spent the 1930–31 academic year at Union Theological Seminary in New York. Back in Berlin he became a lecturer in theology and a student chaplain and was ordained in November 1931; from 1933 he opposed Nazi church policy and helped organise the Pastors' Emergency League. From October 1933 to spring 1935 he was pastor of two German-speaking congregations in London, and he then directed the Confessing Church's preachers' seminary at Zingst and Finkenwalde until the Gestapo closed it in September 1937, continuing the training in Pomeranian collective pastorates until March 1940. Banned from Berlin (1938), from public speaking (1940) and from publishing (1941), he became a civilian agent of the Abwehr (military intelligence) through his brother-in-law Hans von Dohnanyi's circle, and became engaged to Maria von Wedemeyer in January 1943. Arrested on 5 April 1943, he was held in Tegel prison, the Gestapo prison at Prinz-Albrecht-Strasse and Buchenwald, and was hanged at Flossenbürg concentration camp on 9 April 1945, aged 39.

phases.label: Childhood and student years
phases.summary: Born in Breslau, he grew up in Berlin from 1912 and studied theology at Tübingen (from 1923) and Berlin (from 1924). He completed his doctorate with the dissertation Sanctorum Communio in 1927 and passed his first theological examination in January 1928.

phases.label: Barcelona, Berlin, New York
phases.summary: He was vicar to the German Protestant congregation in Barcelona under Pastor Fritz Olbricht from February 1928 to February 1929, then from March 1929 an assistant in the Berlin theology faculty, qualifying as a university teacher with Act and Being in July 1930. From September 1930 to June 1931 he studied at Union Theological Seminary in New York, working regularly at Abyssinian Baptist Church in Harlem.

phases.label: Berlin lecturer and chaplain
phases.summary: Back in Berlin he lectured in theology at the university from August 1931, was ordained in November 1931, served as student chaplain at the Technical College in Charlottenburg and taught a confirmation class in the Zion parish. After Hitler came to power in 1933 he spoke and wrote against Nazi church policy and helped organise the Pastors' Emergency League.

phases.label: London pastorate
phases.summary: From October 1933 until spring 1935 he was pastor of two German-speaking congregations in London, at Sydenham and St Paul's in the East End, living at the parish house at 23 Manor Mount, Forest Hill. He built ties with Bishop George Bell of Chichester and spoke at the Fanø ecumenical conference in August 1934.

phases.label: Zingst and Finkenwalde seminary
phases.summary: From April 1935 he directed the Confessing Church's preachers' seminary, first at Zingst on the Baltic and from June 1935 at Finkenwalde near Stettin, until the Gestapo closed it in September 1937. His authorization to teach at Berlin University was withdrawn in August 1936, and Discipleship was published in November 1937.

phases.label: Pomeranian collective pastorates
phases.summary: From December 1937 he continued training Confessing Church ordinands in collective pastorates at Köslin and Gross-Schlönwitz, moving to Sigurdshof in April 1939, until the Gestapo closed the work in March 1940. Banned from Berlin in January 1938, he wrote Life Together in September 1938 and made a brief trip to the United States in June–July 1939.

phases.label: Abwehr and resistance work
phases.summary: Working for the Abwehr (military intelligence) through his brother-in-law Hans von Dohnanyi's circle, he was attached from November 1940 to its Munich office with stays at Ettal monastery, and travelled to Switzerland, Norway and Sweden, meeting Bishop Bell at Sigtuna in 1942. Banned from public speaking (1940) and publishing (1941), he worked on Ethics and became engaged to Maria von Wedemeyer in January 1943.

phases.label: Imprisonment and execution
phases.summary: Arrested on 5 April 1943, he was held in Tegel military prison in Berlin, where he wrote the letters later published as Letters and Papers from Prison. After incriminating Abwehr files were found in September 1944 he was moved to the Gestapo prison at Prinz-Albrecht-Strasse, then in February 1945 to Buchenwald and finally to Flossenbürg, where he was hanged on 9 April 1945.
